description: Sixteen-step sequencer driven by an incoming phasor rather than a clock, with a voltage knob and a gate button for each step

params.text: Sets how many of the 16 steps the cycle runs through, 1 to 16 in whole numbers
Attenuverts the steps CV input, -1 to +1
Sets the width of the step gates, from 0% to 100% of a step, with 50% at centre
Attenuverts the gate width CV input, -1 to +1
Raw compares the phasor against the gate width directly; Smart mutes the output when the phasor stops and flips the comparison when it runs backwards, keeping reverse phasors in time
Sets the voltage this step sends to the Steps output, -5V to 5V
Turns this step's gate on or off; the lamp shows green when the step is on, blue while it plays, and red when the step is beyond the Steps setting

inputs.text: The phasor that drives the sequence; each 0-10V cycle is divided into the steps
Holds the sequence at the first step below 1V and lets it run at 1V or above; unpatched, the sequence always runs

outputs.text: The voltage of the step playing at that moment
The step voltages with a straight line drawn between them, gliding from one step's voltage to the next across the step
The step voltage captured by the most recent gate, held until the next gate fires
A 10V gate on every step whose gate button is on, at the set width
A 10V trigger at the start of each of those gates

notes: a phasor drives this, not a clock: a ramp rising from 0V to 10V once per cycle, from Phasor Generator, Clock to Phasor or an LFO's saw output. Nothing moves here until one is patched in.
every step gate starts switched off, so no gates or triggers come out until you switch at least one step on; the step voltage outputs follow the phasor either way.
